_note: Movement constants in HAMMER UNITS (1 hu = 1 inch = 0.0254 m), which is how the engine stores them. src/game/movement.ts converts once. Sources and confidence are in docs/FIDELITY.md; almost all of these are engine defaults rather than estimates.
_slideTurn: How fast a slide can be steered, degrees a second, turning the velocity you already have rather than adding to it. A slide could only be nudged before: the wish added acceleration along itself, which over a short slide is a drift rather than a turn, so a slide held its line and you took corners by ending it. Turning the vector keeps the speed, which is what carving is.
_mantleCarry: How much of the speed you arrived at a ledge with comes out on top of it, 0 to 1, along the way you were facing. A mantle used to spend all of it: you arrived on the ledge standing still and had to build the speed again, which made a run of ledges read as a series of climbs rather than one movement. Capped at a sprint, so a slide into a ledge does not launch you off the top of it.
_extra: Movement this game does not have by default, and did not want by default: a double jump and a wall run. The owner asked for both after playing a round of Crown, and both change how every fight reads, so they are OFF here and turned on per match in the lobby (the Movement box). Everything else in this file is Apex's, measured; these two are ours, and are kept apart from it for that reason.

extra._doubleJump: one more jump while in the air, at `height` hu against the ground jump's 56, once until you touch ground, a wall or a rope again. `grace` is how long after leaving the ground it is refused, so a mistimed ground jump does not eat it.
extra._wallRun: a run along a wall you are moving along in the air: it holds you against the wall for up to `seconds`, falling at `fall` of gravity (a bit over half, so a run carries you along and lifts you a little rather than walking you up the side of a building), and you leave it with a jump that throws you `out` hu off the wall and `up` hu up. `minSpeed` is how fast you have to be going along the wall to start one, so walking into a wall does not stick you to it (a walk is 173 hu/s and a sprint 260, and what is left of either in the air after a jump is less, so this sits under a walk), and `cooldown` is how long before the same wall takes you again, which is what stops a wall being a ladder.

_hull: Collision capsule. Standing height is the medium-legend value; every legend crouches to the same height.
_ground: Ground movement is accelerate-to-target in three bands, NOT Quake friction: lowAcceleration below lowSpeed, acceleration up to sprintBandStart, sprintAcceleration above it. Holding a weapon halves all of it (armedAccelScale). The wiki (Advanced Slide Tech): 0.35 s from standing to 200 hu/s with a weapon out, twice the 0.12 s holstered, and 0.45 s to 207. The band values are a fit to those three timings; lowAcceleration keeps the engine value.
_air: Air movement IS Quake-style, with no friction or drag at all. airSpeed is the max wish speed and is double the classic Source value, which is why air strafing gains speed so fast.
_slideJump: The wiki's velocity table: a slide jump is 475 hu/s on its first frame, out of the 400 hu/s slide cap, so its vertical part is sqrt(475^2 - 400^2) = 256 hu/s and it peaks 256^2 / (2 x 750) = 43.7 hu up. That apex is inside the green zone (19 to 47), which is why the basic wallbounce is a SLIDE jump: a plain jump peaks at 56, above it.
_jumpFatigue: A jump within antiMultiJumpTimeMin of landing is cut to antiMultiJumpHeightFrac of full height, recovering linearly to full by antiMultiJumpTimeMax. The timer starts on LANDING.
_skip: Bunny-hop penalty: jumping within skipTime of landing loses speed, but never below skipSpeedRetain.
_slide: The slide boost is instant and capped, friction is 12.5x gentler than standing, and a slide jump only keeps its speed if taken below slideMaxJumpSpeed OR at least slideJumpGraceTime into the slide.
_mantle: Auto-mantle up to mantleHeight. Duration is bucketed by how high the ledge is relative to the player, not by approach speed.
_crouchTiming: Crouching takes effect after a delay; standing up is instant. Both are instant while sliding.
_crouchVisual: Ours: the view moves between standing and crouched height at a steady rate that takes crouchVisualTime for the whole distance. The slide starts on the frame crouch is pressed; the view has to keep up with it.
_crouchStandVisual: From the wiki's crouch timing: when standing, the crouched state arrives crouchDelay (0.4 s) after the press, once the crouch animation has finished, and standing back up is instant. So a standing crouch lowers the VIEW over the 0.4 s from the press and shrinks the HULL when the state flips; a slide drops both in crouchVisualTime; standing up raises the view in crouchVisualTime.
_climb: Apex climbing, from the Apex Movement Wiki (apexmovement.tech, Climb Fundamentals and Climb Space). You must leave the ground first, face the wall within 45.57 degrees (arccos 0.7), and push into it. Climbing is limited by whichever comes first: the CLIMB SPACE, which starts at your feet at your last ground contact and ends 147 hu higher, or the ATTACH OFFSET, 100 hu above where you attached. Reaching either throws you 28 hu further up (the end boost). Upward climbing peaks at 225 hu/s on mouse and keyboard; up or down climbing moves at most 115 hu/s sideways, a pure sideways climb 258 hu/s for at most 1 s. Crouch, backwards, or turning more than 45.57 degrees away detaches you and drops the climb space by 128 hu; jumping off drops it by 128 from the bottom 19 hu (mini zone) or 256 above that, and gives 28.21 hu of height plus 188 (mini) or 258 hu/s away from the wall. You cannot reattach to the same wall until you drop below your previous attach point.
_climbZones: Climb zones (Apex Movement Wiki, Climb Zones). The climb space is split into the mini zone (baseline to 19 hu), the green zone (19 to 47 hu) and the neutral zone (47 hu to the 147 hu cutoff). Jumping off a climb: from the mini zone, 28.21 hu of height and 188 hu/s out, the normal 128 hu penalty (a mini-bounce); from the green zone, more height the LOWER you are in it and 258 hu/s out, 256 hu penalty (a wallbounce); from the neutral zone, no added height, only 258 hu/s out, 256 hu penalty, carrying whatever vertical speed you had (a wall push).
_climbGreen: From the wiki's velocity table (Wall dismounts): a wall bounce is 484 hu/s at most and 350 at least on its first frame, with 258 of it horizontal, so the vertical part runs from 409 hu/s at the bottom of the green zone to 236 at its top (the wiki: the lower you are in the zone, the more height), linear between. Mini bounce 278 = 188 out plus 205 up (28.21 hu). Crouch kick 320: a mini bounce with crouch pressed on the same frame, 245 out.
_climbApprox: Not documented, ours: how quickly a climb reaches its 225 hu/s (climbAccel), and that a pure sideways climb holds height rather than rising.
_lurch: Lurch, from the Apex Movement Wiki (Lurch Fundamentals). A window of 400 ms opens when you press jump. Pressing a direction key inside it redirects your velocity; releasing a key does not, and a key held before the jump does not. Full strength for the first 200 ms, then linear decay to zero at 400 ms. The new direction is the combination of every direction key held at the moment of the press, so holding left and pressing right is a null lurch. Strength sets both the direction change and the speed lost. Above roughly 1150-1300 hu/s lurch stops working. The redirect is a blend of the velocity toward (speed x new direction) by lurchStrength x fade; a blend rather than a rotation is what produces the documented speed loss on wide angles and almost none on the small angles a tap-strafe uses.
_superglide: Superglide, from the Apex Movement Wiki. In the last 0.15 s of a mantle, press jump and then crouch exactly one frame later. Out of a sprint you get a slide boost and a jump together, in the air, so no ground friction eats it. Out of a walk the window is about the last 0.01 s and the speed is lower (the reduced speed is ours: walk speed plus the boost).
_superglideHeight: The wiki's velocity table: a superglide is about 540 hu/s on its first frame, out of the 400 hu/s slide cap, so its vertical part is sqrt(540^2 - 400^2) = 363 hu/s and it peaks 363^2 / (2 x 750) = 87.8 hu up. That is why a superglide reaches ledges a jump cannot.
_fallstun: Fall stun, from the Apex Movement Wiki (Fundamental Air Tech). Landing from a 300 hu fall (7.6 m) gives none; from 800 hu (20.3 m) a full 1 s stun and full velocity loss. It scales with landing SPEED, the speed a free fall from those heights would reach, and grows faster than linearly (the wiki suspects quadratic; we use quadratic). The acceleration penalty during the stun is not published; ours is fallstunAccelScale.
_sprintBuffer: Apex's default sprint is PRESS, not hold. Pressing sprint arms it for up to 3 s until you move forward, and a running sprint keeps it armed. Letting go of forward ends the sprint and needs a new press. Sprinting works only up to 45 degrees either side of forward.
_mantleInput: A mantle needs your movement input pointing at the wall within 50 degrees either side (cos 50 = 0.643).
_slideAir: A slide on landing needs BOTH 90 hu/s horizontal AND 200 hu/s downward. Checking only the horizontal let a gentle hop turn into a slide.
_slideSlope: Downward slopes reduce slide friction and can reverse it; upward slopes increase it. The along-slope part of gravity is g*sin(theta), and sin(theta) is the rate of height change over the speed, so this needs no surface normal.
_slideFriction: Refit to the two slide timings the Apex Movement Wiki measured: a slide started just over 200 hu/s drops below 350 in about 0.11-0.12 s, and a full holstered-sprint slide (460) drops below 350 in 0.21 s. No single linear friction meets both; a gentle base (slideDecel, 100 hu/s2) plus a fast shed of any speed ABOVE 350 does. The old 100 + 0.7 x speed met neither and killed slides early. slideVelocityDecay stays as the engine value it is, but the fitted shed rate is what the controller uses.
_viewFeel: Camera. The landing dip is ours and cosmetic. The sprint FOV kick and strafe roll that were here are gone: Apex does neither, and they were my additions, not the game's.
_zipline: Ziplines, from the Apex Movement Wiki (Zipline Basics, Zip Jump, Zip Crouch). Interact to ride, in the direction you look; near a pole you are forced away from it. Top speed 600 hu/s (vertical zips 480), previous momentum along the zip is kept up to that. Engine values: ziplineAcceleration 400, ziplineJumpOnAcceleration 1000, mountZiplineTime 0.5, useZiplineCooldown 0.4, ziplineJumpOffSpeed 400, ziplineJumpOffDampScale 1. A manual disconnect (jump or crouch) leaves at up to 445 hu/s, riding to the end at up to 600. Zips steeper than 45 degrees let you jump off in any direction; shallower ones throw you off along the zip whatever you look at. The interact prompt shows when you face the zip within 35 degrees on the ground, 90 in the air, or look straight up or down in the air. No ground interact while aiming. Three mid-air interacts, reset by touching the ground or mantling, and one more back after 3 s off a zip. Hitting geometry throws you off. Riding 0.5 s resets the climb space. A zip jump is not a jump: no jump fatigue.
_ziplineOurs: Not documented, ours: the interact reach from your hands to the rope (ziplineReach), how far below the rope your feet hang (ziplineHang: standing height plus a forearm), how long the pull onto the rope takes at most (ziplinePullTime), what counts as near a pole (ziplinePoleZone), the upward pop of a zip jump (the wiki says slight; we use the climb jump's 28.21 hu), the pitch that counts as looking straight up or down (ziplineAirPitchDeg), and the forward push when a zip crouch or the top of a steep zip drops you (ziplineSteepExitPush).
